summary: We developed a website, AstroHealth Alert, that would utilize real-time data to track the astronauts health and prevent possible life-threatening injuries. The challenge was to create a health monitoring software and AstroHealth Alert does exactly that. It monitors the astronauts health but also interprets it so that the astronaut can take reasonable action to prevent health injuries. Messages being delivered from space to Earth would take a significant amount of time and could threaten the astronauts health further. AstroHealth Alert is real time and would advise the astronaut to take immediate precaution when their health is at risk.
details: AstroHealth Alert utilizes real-time health data gathered from pre-existing health monitoring devices and tracks it as a graph on its website. It tracks 5 different health indicators: heart rate, sleep duration, fatigue, radiation exposure, and days spent in space. There are 3 different status bars to indicate whether or not the astronauts health is in danger: green indicates the health is okay, yellow indicates the health is at risk and red indicates the health is in danger and the astronaut needs medical attention. Unfortuantely, we couldn't find any public databases to access real astronauts health data so we instead used simulated data from MATLAB to showcase the idea. AstroHealth Alert would use the collected data and interpret whether or not the astronaut's health is at risk. If the astronaut's health is in critical danger, AstroHealth Alert would prompt immediate action and advise the astronaut to take preventative care such as seeking nearest shelter to avoid further radiation exposure. Furthermore, if the astronaunt's health is at risk, as indicated by a yellow status bar, AstroHealth Alert would begin sending warning messages to Earth to quickstart medical care. AstroHealth Alert would signicantly reduce health risks on space missions and help astronauts stay safe. This is significant and we chose to work on this challenge because health risks in space are different then on Earth. It is harder to be treated while in space and astronauts are completing missions that can change humanity for the better. By monitoring their health and making sure nobody gets hurt, we hope to make a siginicant impact in making their missions easier since the astronauts don't have to worry about the possibility of becoming fatally sick. We used MATLAB, with the help of Copilot, to simulate data that would reflect the real-life data from astronauts. We then developed the website using HTML and CSS on Visual Studio Code. Our project's creativeness lies in the graphic design of the website and how we built on pre-existing health monitoring devices to help monitor astronauts health. Factors our team considered are how there are already devices such as Garmin and Biomonitor that exists on the market. However, those devices only monitors the biometrics; AstroHealth Alert takes those data, interprets it, communicates it to the astronaut in real time, and also sends the information to NASA as soon as the astronauts health is at risk so NASA can have adequate time to send medical help before the astronauts health is in danger.
